reasons.reason: A 3 by 3 grid has four grid lines in each direction, and at each of the four crossing stages you choose an order of moves, so counting the orderings gives four factorial, which is 24 paths.
Crossing a 3 by 3 grid of squares takes exactly three moves right and three moves up, so each path is just a choice of which three of the six moves go right, giving 20.
Squaring the sum of the square roots of 7 and 5 gives 7 plus 5 plus twice the square root of 35, which is exactly 12 plus 2 root 35.
The 12 under the radical points to 2 root 3, since its square is 12, and root 35 contains a factor of root 5, so pairing 2 root 3 with root 5 fits the structure.
By Vieta, a quartic's root product equals the constant term over the leading coefficient, with a plus sign because the degree is even, so here it comes to 5 over 1.
Vieta's last relation ties the root product to the coefficient sitting just before the constant, and that x term has magnitude 10, with the even degree cancelling any minus sign.
Since omega cubed is 1, the four factors reduce to two copies of the pair with omega and omega squared, and each pair expands to 1 plus omega plus omega squared plus 1, which is 2.
Reducing powers mod 3, omega to the fourth is omega and omega to the eighth is omega squared, and each pair product equals 2 plus omega plus omega squared, which is 1, so the whole thing is 1.

A right triangle has probability zero here, so every random triangle is either acute or obtuse, and with the points placed symmetrically around the circle neither outcome is favoured, giving one half.
The triangle is acute exactly when the centre lies inside it, and for each of the three arcs the chance it exceeds a semicircle is one quarter, leaving one minus three quarters.
